title: Gate DONE on the delivery evidence the project policy requires
description:
Objective: close the defect the roadmap reproduced against the real handlers. Task A reaches DONE with completionCommits empty and only a soft NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT warning, and a worker then successfully claims a task that depends on A.

Deliverable: a deliveryPolicy setting in .moe/project.json declaring what DONE requires: local branch commit, remote branch push, merged pull request, or an explicit manual artifact. qa_approve turns today's soft warning into a hard refusal when the recorded evidence does not satisfy the configured policy, naming exactly which evidence is missing. The default policy must reproduce today's behaviour so no existing project changes on upgrade, and the setting is what opts a project into strictness.

Not in scope: the receipt record and target-movement recheck, which is the sibling task, and the dependent-claim gate, which is another. Preserve autoCommit=false and manual or no-git projects: under those the manual-artifact policy applies and missing code evidence is labelled as such, never reported as verified delivery.

Verification: npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: A deliveryPolicy setting supports local branch, remote push, merged pull request and manual artifact, documented in docs/CONFIGURATION.md
qa_approve hard-refuses when the recorded evidence does not satisfy the configured policy, and the error names the specific missing evidence
The default policy preserves today's soft-warning behaviour exactly, proven by the existing qa_approve tests staying green unmodified
Under the manual-artifact policy a task with no commit reaches DONE only with a recorded artifact, and its state labels the evidence as manual rather than verified delivery
autoCommit=false projects keep working and are covered by a test
npx vitest run src/tools/qaApprove.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: The default must be behaviour-preserving; strictness is opt-in via settings.
Never label missing code evidence as verified delivery.

LANDED EVIDENCE, used verbatim:
- Candidates: state.candidates, via listCandidatesForTask(state, taskId). The list is sorted by createdAt then id, and its LAST entry is the current candidate. That is the same rule getContext.currentCandidate and resolveReviewedCandidate use.
- Check runs: state.checkRuns (.moe/checks), via listCheckRunsForCandidate(state, candidateId), which returns copies in createdAt-then-id order. CheckRun fields: {id, candidateId, treeSha, command (verbatim), exitCode, outputTail, runnerId, source: 'runner-observed'|'agent-reported', createdAt?}.
- Commits: TaskCommit {kind: completion|checkpoint|rescue, pushed?: boolean (record_commit only ever upgrades it to true), recordedAt ISO}.
- Missing today: task.prLink means a PR was opened (complete_task, PR_OPENED activity); nothing records a PR merge. No manual-artifact field exists, and StateManager has no receipts map (b1c98508 has not landed).
- Settings: normalizeProject spreads unknown keys, so deliveryPolicy survives load. validateSettingsUpdate rejects unknown keys, as it already does for staleWorkerTimeoutMs, reconcileWindowMs and models, and both IDEs send fixed keys only. So deliveryPolicy is a project.json key validated where it is used, by the resolver.
- Wrapper gate conditions (moe-agent.sh:6399-6428, ps1:3182-3186): the gate runs only on a completion landing with autoCommit on and a trimmed, non-blank qualityGate. Any scope other than everyTask counts as epicFinal and is deferred unless the task is epic-final (the getContext.ts:244 rule). The check requirement MUST mirror these conditions, or a strict policy would demand a check no runner ever produces.

CONFLICT FOUND, AND HOW I RESOLVED IT:
- The problem: criterion 2's P is DONE with NO task.commits (only candidate, review, receipt and check records). It must yield exactly ['required-check:node gate.cjs'], then [] once the runner-observed pass is recorded. A predicate that demanded commit-ledger evidence from a DONE task would break a held-out assertion neither card may edit, and receipts are out of scope here.
- The rule: landing evidence (commit, push, merged-PR or manual artifact) is a DONE-TRANSITION requirement, judged for any status except DONE and ARCHIVED, which in practice is the REVIEW task qa_approve sees. The required check binds to the current candidate's immutable records and is judged for EVERY status.
- It is one function with no caller options, so qa_approve and the dependency gate cannot disagree.
- Recording point for manual artifact and merged PR: none exists. qa_approve gains optional attestations, accepted only under the matching policy, and persists task.deliveryEvidence {kind, reference, verifiedDelivery: false, recordedBy, recordedAt}.

TOKENS:
- Evidence tokens: completion-commit, pushed-completion-commit, merged-pull-request, manual-artifact, required-check:<trimmed qualityGate>.
- Policy values: legacy (the default, also used when the setting is absent or null), local-branch, remote-push, merged-pull-request, manual-artifact. Anything else is refused as INVALID_INPUT.
- Refusal: -32003 DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, the same numeric code as DEPENDENCY_EVIDENCE_MISSING. Its context is {taskId, deliveryPolicy, missingEvidence}, and the message carries the tokens because MoeError.context is not forwarded over the wire.

implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE POLICY MODULE AS A REUSABLE PREDICATE. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts as the single authority for what DONE requires. Export the recognised policy values — the behaviour-preserving default plus local branch commit, remote branch push, merged pull request and manual artifact — a resolver that reads `deliveryPolicy` from project settings and refuses an unrecognised value as invalid input rather than falling back to the default, and the stable token vocabulary as exported constants or builders so no caller ever hand-writes a token string. The required-check token MUST render exactly as criterion 2 asserts, the prefix followed by the gate command, so build it from the `qualityGate` setting through a named builder and test it against that literal. Export ONE evidence function taking the state and any task and returning whether that task satisfies the configured policy plus the list of missing evidence tokens. It must be a plain predicate over a task, because task-94f53492 consumes it for a PREREQUISITE task rather than for the task being approved; a closure shaped around the approval path would force that card to copy the rules, which is precisely what its four decoy records exist to catch. Evidence rules: the commit-shaped requirements read the task's recorded commits using the same at-or-after-reviewStartedAt filter qa_approve already applies, so a stale earlier-attempt commit never satisfies a later review; the pushed and merged-pull-request requirements need their own distinguishing evidence rather than treating any commit as delivery; the manual requirement needs a recorded artifact and nothing else may stand in for it; and the check requirement, when the gate scope demands one for this task, needs a check bound to the task's CURRENT candidate, that candidate's own tree, the required command, a zero exit and a runner-observed source. Error handling is fail-closed throughout: an unreadable record, an unresolvable candidate or any lookup failure reports the evidence MISSING and never falls through to satisfied, because a rail forbids labelling missing code evidence as verified delivery. Return tokens only for what is actually missing, so a satisfied policy returns an empty list.

implementationPlan.description: TURN THE SOFT WARNING INTO A CONDITIONAL HARD REFUSAL. In packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/qaApprove.ts, resolve the policy and evaluate the evidence through the new module, then branch on the result. Under the default policy change NOTHING: the existing warning string, the singular warning key, the warnings array and the DONE transition all behave exactly as today, because a rail makes strictness opt-in and an existing project must see no difference on upgrade. Under a configured policy that the evidence does not satisfy, throw an error naming the specific missing evidence tokens and carrying them in its context alongside the task id and the resolved policy, so a human reads which evidence is absent rather than a generic refusal. Place the refusal with the other hard gates already in this handler — after the read, ownership, summary and reviewed-candidate guards so their precedence is unchanged, and before the Review write, the task update, the worker touch and every chat side effect, so a refused approval moves not one byte and leaves the reviews directory empty. Follow the shape of the neighbouring finalizing and candidate refusals for consistency on the wire. Under the manual-artifact policy, when the recorded artifact IS present, let the approval proceed and persist an explicit label on the task recording that DONE rested on a manual artifact rather than on verified delivery — an additive optional field, no migration, and the wording must not read as a verified landing, which is what the second rail is about. Keep the soft warnings flowing in every case that still reaches DONE, including under a satisfied strict policy, since they carry information the refusal no longer needs to.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Shaping the evidence check as a can-this-task-go-DONE closure inside qaApprove.ts: rejected, and this is the decision that justified taking this card now. task-94f53492 is already planned to consume this helper for a PREREQUISITE task, and its acceptance case plants four decoy check records specifically to catch a second subtly different implementation. A closure around the approval path would force that copy, so the helper is a plain predicate over any task in its own module. (2) Letting this card cover only commit-shaped evidence and leaving the check dimension to the dependency card: rejected for the same reason — the two plans would then contradict each other, since the dependency card was explicitly told not to reimplement the rules. The helper covers both dimensions and this card owns the token vocabulary. (3) Falling back to the default policy on an unrecognised setting value: rejected outright. A project that misspells a strict policy would silently keep reporting unverified work as delivered, which is the exact defect the card exists to close, so an unknown value is invalid input. (4) Treating any recorded commit as satisfying the pushed and merged-pull-request policies: rejected — each needs its own distinguishing evidence or the stricter policies are decorative. (5) Making the default policy strict, or warning louder under it: forbidden by a rail; strictness is opt-in and the soft path stays because the wrapper legitimately lands the commit after complete_task returns. (6) Adding a receipt record to carry the manual artifact: out of scope by the card's own wording; the manual label is an additive optional field on the task.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: qa_approve has already grown two hard gates from siblings landed earlier in this epic: an attempt-finalizing refusal and a reviewed-candidate binding, both placed before every mutation, which is the precedent and the position for this one. Its existing soft commit gate already computes exactly the evidence this card needs to reuse — completion commits filtered to at or after reviewStartedAt so a stale earlier-attempt commit cannot satisfy a later review, plus checkpoint and rescue commits and an autoCommit-on flag — and its comment records WHY it is soft: the wrapper lands the commit seconds after complete_task, so a fast approval can legitimately arrive first. That reasoning must survive under the default policy. The strict fixture in the acceptance file sets deliveryPolicy alongside the ALREADY EXISTING qualityGate and qualityGateScope settings, so the required gate command and whether this task needs one both come from settings that predate this epic. src/delivery/ currently holds only the acceptance test, so policy.ts is the natural home and is what the dependency card's plan already refers to as the helper it consumes. Acceptance criterion 2 pins one token byte for byte, the required-check prefix followed by the gate command, and its four decoys define the check-matching rule: current candidate, that candidate's own tree, the required command, zero exit, runner-observed source.
planningNotes.risks: The highest-impact failure is silent non-strictness: an unrecognised policy value quietly treated as the default leaves a project believing DONE is gated when it is not, so that path must be invalid input. Second, the default must be untouched, and the proof is the existing qa_approve cases passing unmodified — any edit to one means default behaviour moved. Third, the whole test suite boots projects with no delivery policy at all, so a resolver that throws on an absent setting fails broadly; absent means default. Fourth, the required-check token is asserted deep-equal by another card's acceptance case, so a single character of drift breaks a consumer that this plan forbids from writing its own token. Fifth, fail-open is the dangerous direction everywhere in this module: an unreadable record must read as missing evidence, never as satisfied, and nothing may describe absent code evidence as verified delivery. Finally, state the boundary honestly: this gate reads RECORDED evidence and re-runs nothing, so a commit or check record that misreports what happened still satisfies the policy — binding a record to an observed run belongs to the runner and receipt cards.

NEW packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts is the single authority: a plain predicate over ANY task. evaluateDeliveryEvidence(state, task, attestations?) returns {policy, satisfied, missingEvidence}. task-94f53492 consumes the token vocabulary through EVIDENCE_TOKENS / requiredCheckToken: completion-commit, pushed-completion-commit, merged-pull-request, manual-artifact, required-check:<trimmed qualityGate>. Rules:
- Absent/null = legacy. The soft NO-COMPLETION-COMMIT gate is unchanged on purpose: the wrapper lands commits after the CLI exits. An unknown value is INVALID_INPUT.
- local-branch: completion commit at/after reviewStartedAt. remote-push: one recorded pushed. merged-pull-request / manual-artifact: an attestation to qa_approve, accepted only under its own policy, persisted as task.deliveryEvidence {verifiedDelivery:false}.
- Landing is judged only before DONE, because criterion 2's DONE P has no commits. The required check (current candidate, its tree, gate command, exit 0, runner-observed, only when the wrapper runs the gate) is judged in every status.
- The refusal comes before any write: -32003 DELIVERY_EVIDENCE_MISSING, context {taskId, deliveryPolicy, missingEvidence}, message naming each token.
